Screen
The term "screen" in this context refers to various web page components within a digital marketplace environment, each identified by unique IDs and titles, serving different purposes within the platform. Examples include the "home" screen titled "One Stop Market," which acts as the store's homepage, accessible via the URL "http://localhost:7770/". Another screen, labeled "cart_empty," represents an empty shopping cart, located at "http://localhost:7770/checkout/cart/", indicating the absence of items in the cart. Additionally, there is a "category" screen under the title "Electronics," which lists electronics products, accessible through the URL "http://localhost:7770/electronics.html". A "minicart_open" screen displays a mini-cart dropdown after an item has been added to the cart, with the URL pointing back to the homepage at "http://localhost:7770/". The "cart_with_item" screen shows the shopping cart after an item has been added, reflecting the updated cart contents.

Furthermore, other forms such as an "advanced search form," a "customer login form artifact," and a "guest orders and returns form screen" are also categorized under the term "screen." These forms serve specific functions within the platform, facilitating user interaction and navigation. Another example is the "search_empty" screen artifact with ID 'search_empty', title "Search results for: 'zzzxxyynotfound999'", and description 'Search with zero results', located at "http://localhost:7770/catalogsearch/result/?q=zzzxxyynotfound999". Additionally, there is a "subcategory" screen artifact with ID 'subcategory', title 'Cell Phones & Accessories', described as a subcategory via navigation click from Electronics, and has a URL pointing to "http://localhost:7770/cell-phones-accessories.html". The "register" screen with the ID 'register', title 'Create New Customer Account', and a description 'Create customer account form', can be accessed at "http://localhost:7770/customer/account/create/". The "account_logged_in" screen artifact with ID 'account_logged_in', title 'My Account', and description 'My Account after UI login', is located at "http://localhost:7770/customer/account/". Lastly, the "search_results" screen artifact with ID 'search_results', title "Search results for: 'shirt'", and description "Search results for 'shirt'", is found at "http://localhost:7770/search?query=shirt".

screen_id
The entity "screen_id" is a versatile identifier used to denote different sections of a user interface, including the home screen and the search results screen. These screens play crucial roles in guiding user navigation and providing relevant information within the application. The home screen is a fundamental part of the user interface, serving as the starting point for navigation within the application. It is often the first screen users encounter when launching the app and has an associated ID, which can be either "home" or "search_results," depending on its function. This ID helps in locating and referencing specific parts of the interface programmatically.

The search results screen is another significant component of the interface, used to display the outcomes of a search query, providing users with relevant information or content. Like the home screen, it also has an ID, which can be "search_results" or "home," indicating its role in the overall structure of the application. The search results screen serves as a location identifier, facilitating easy access to the results through a unique ID.

Additionally, "screen_id" is a unique identifier for a screen in a user interface and can refer to a screen element with an ID of "search_results." It can also serve as a location identifier for the search results screen. Furthermore, there are mentions of "screen_id" being an identifier for a specific screen element, with values such as "search_advanced." Overall, "screen_id" is a critical component in defining and navigating through the various sections of a user interface, ensuring a seamless and efficient user experience.<SEP>A screen ID with the value 'subcategory'.<SEP>Unique identifier for a screen element<SEP>A screen ID with the value 'search_advanced'.<SEP>A screen element with ID 'search_advanced'

instruction
The term "instruction" generally refers to various actions involving clicking on specific elements within a user interface. These instructions can include selecting items such as "Electronics," "Beauty & Personal Care," or interacting with menu items, buttons, links, and comboboxes. An instruction typically involves clicking on a designated element to perform a specific action, such as searching for products or navigating through different categories. In some contexts, an instruction may also encompass the act of clicking to execute a broader method or action within a system. Instructions can be seen as commands to perform an action, actions to click a link, or sets of steps or commands given to a user. Examples of specific instructions include clicking the menu item "Sports & Outdoors" or "Beauty & Personal Care," and actions like signing in. Additionally, "click instruction" specifically refers to the act of clicking a menu item, while "clicking action to select 'Health & Household'" is a more specific example of an instruction. A "set of instructions" encompasses a series of actions that need to be performed sequentially, often involving interactions with various elements on a user interface.<SEP>A command or set of instructions.<SEP>An instruction to click a menu item.<SEP>An instruction to click a link.<SEP>Set of actions to perform<SEP>An instruction to click the menu item 'Video Games'.

role
The term "role" is versatile and can denote various functions depending on the context. In the realm of user interfaces, a role can signify the specific function of a menu item, button, or link, indicating its intended use or behavior. For instance, a role might specify the function of a link, such as navigating to a particular page or performing an action. Similarly, a role can be assigned to elements like a combobox, defining their intended use or behavior. Additionally, roles can be associated with specific menu items, such as "Sports & Outdoors" or "Beauty & Personal Care," providing context-specific functions. The term "role" can also refer to a designation for a specific function, often related to accessibility. It is important to note that while some descriptions mention attributes related to links, these do not directly define the role itself. A role or function can be associated with an element, a menu item, or a concept related to the role of the combobox. bbox_px
bbox_px refers to the bounding box coordinates of various graphical elements such as buttons, links, and menu items, measured in pixels. This term specifically denotes the pixel coordinates of the bounding box for a button, a link, and a menu item, indicating the area encompassing these interactive elements on a screen. It ensures accurate placement and sizing of graphical components in digital interfaces. bbox_px can also refer to the pixel coordinates of the combobox, a bounding box in pixel coordinates, bounding box coordinates, bounding box coordinates in pixels, bounding box coordinates in pixel units, and bounding box pixel coordinates for the product image container. Pixel coordinates of the menu item 'Beauty & Personal Care' and pixel coordinates of the combobox are mentioned, further emphasizing the use of bbox_px in specifying precise locations and dimensions of graphical elements in digital interfaces. a11y
The term "a11y" is an abbreviation for accessibility, a multifaceted approach aimed at ensuring that digital content and interfaces are usable by individuals with disabilities. It encompasses both technical aspects, such as accessibility features and user interface elements, and organizational affiliations dedicated to accessibility initiatives. The term is commonly used to describe accessibility in various contexts, including source elements for accessibility instructions. For instance, in a screen interaction with ID "home," the term "a11y" might refer to a clickable link with detailed instructions and bounding box positions, such as the "Belle Of The Ball Princess Sprinkle Mix" link, which has a role of "link" and a bounding box position of [779, 674, 1002, 793]. Similarly, in another screen interaction with ID "search_results," the term could relate to accessibility features for web applications, such as instructions to click the menu for different categories. Additionally, "a11y" is associated with an organization focused on accessibility initiatives, highlighting its significance in promoting digital inclusivity. The term is also linked to accessibility-related elements and methods, further underscoring its importance in enhancing usability for people with disabilities.<SEP>[a11y] is a term related to accessibility and usability in web development.
